chunks: Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who cultivated a crop, whether he was a Muslim or a confederate (dhimmi), and spent expenditure on it. Then it became necessary for him to sell it due to his relocation from his place or for a need. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should buy it with silver (dirhams), for its origin is foodstuff.'

key_terms.مُعَاهَداً: Confederate / Dhimmi (non-Muslim living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling green crops for silver currency in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of selling unharvested crops (*al-ba'i bi-al-ba'i*) by establishing that since the primary nature of the plant is foodstuff, it is treated as a commodity that can be sold for silver (*dirhams*) without the strict restrictions applied to gold-for-gold or silver-for-silver exchanges. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the intrinsic value of food and other monetary commodities, ensuring that agricultural transactions remain valid and free from usury (*riba*) concerns.

en.hubeali: Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who cultivated a farm of one who was a Muslim or a confederate. So he spent therein some expenditure, then it became inevitable for him to sell it due to his relocation from his place, or a need of his. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should buy it with the silver (Dirhams), for its origin is foodstuff’.
en.sarwar: 8. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

Upon my asking him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who establishes a plantation, who is a Muslim or tax payer, maintains it and incurs expenses on it, then he decides to sell it because of his relocating or other needs. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can buy it (with al-warzq, as leaves not as grains) because its origin is from foodstuff.’”
